# Campfire

Campfire is a web-based chat application. It supports many of the features you'd
expect, including:

- Multiple rooms, with access controls
- Direct messages
- File attachments with previews
- Search
- Notifications (via Web Push)
- @mentions

## Running your own Campfire instance

Campfire's Docker image contains everything needed for a fully-functional,
single-machine deployment. This includes the web app, background jobs, caching,
file serving, and SSL. You can use our pre-built image at
`ghcr.io/basecamp/once-campfire:latest`, or build your own from this repo.

### Deploying with ONCE

The easiest way to self-host Campfire is with [ONCE](https://github.com/basecamp/once).
It will guide you through the initial set up and then keep your instance up to date automatically.

If you don't already have `once` installed, run this on the machine you want to run Campfire on:

```sh
curl https://get.once.com | sh
```

`once` will launch as soon as the install is finished. 

Choose Campfire from the list of applications, follow the instructions, and ONCE will take care of the rest.

If you prefer the command line to the dashboard, you can deploy directly:

```sh
once deploy ghcr.io/basecamp/once-campfire --host chat.example.com
```

### Deploying with Docker

If you'd rather run the Docker image yourself, you can read more about that in the [self-hosting guide](docs/self-hosting.md).

> [!TIP]
> When you start Campfire for the first time, you'll be guided through a wizard to create an admin account.
> The email address that you enter for the admin account will be visible on the sign-in page, it's there so
> that people have someone to contact if they need help with their account. If that bothers you, put in any
> email address you want and create yourself a new admin account.

## Development

You are welcome - and encouraged - to modify Campfire to your liking.
Please see our [development guide](docs/development.md) for how to get Campfire set up for local development.

## Security

See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for how to report a vulnerability and a description of our trust model.
# How to contribute to Campfire

Campfire uses GitHub
[discussions](https://github.com/basecamp/once-campfire/discussions) to track
feature requests and questions, rather than [the issue
tracker](https://github.com/basecamp/once-campfire/issues). If you're considering
opening an issue or pull request, please open a discussion instead.

Whenever a discussion leads to an actionable and well-understood task, we'll
move it to the issue tracker where it can be worked on.

This is a little different than how some other projects work, but it makes it
easier for us to triage and prioritise the work. It also means that the open
issues all represent agreed-upon tasks that are either being worked on, or are
ready to be worked on.

This should also make it easier to see what's in progress, and to find
something to work on if you'd like to do so.

## What this means in practice

### If you'd like to contribute to the code...

1. If you're interested in working on one of the open issues, please do! We are
   grateful for the help!
2. You'll want to make sure someone else isn't already working on the same
   issue. If they are, it will be tagged "in progress" and/or it should be clear
   from the comments. When in doubt, you can always comment on the issue to ask.
3. Similarly, if you need any help or guidance on the issue, please comment on
   the issue as you go, and we'll do our best to help.
4. When you have something ready for review or collaboration, open a PR.

### If you've found a bug...

1. If you don't have steps to reproduce the problem, or you're not certain it's a
   bug, open a discussion.
2. If you have steps to reproduce, open an issue.

### If you have an idea for a feature...

1. Open a discussion.

### If you have a question, or are having trouble with configuration...

1. Open a discussion.

Hopefully this process makes it easier for everyone to be involved. Thanks for
helping! ❤️

into rooms (`curl -d "Deploy of v1.2.3 finished ✅" https://chat.example.com/rooms/<room-id>/<bot-code>/messages`).

This document records the decisions behind the feature, so that changes to it start from the same
understanding.

## How it fits together

- **Bots are users.** `Bot < User`, a single-table-inheritance subclass stored in the `users` table
  (`users.type = 'Bot'`). Memberships, message authorship, avatars, mentions, unread tracking and push
  notifications all key off `User`, so bots reuse them without any special cases.
- **Owner:** `users.creator_id` is the person who created the bot. `User has_many :bots`.
- **Credential:** `users.bot_key` is the bot code: 32 random alphanumeric characters, unique, and
  shown on the bots page. It's the only thing the API checks.
- **Password:** `users.password_digest` is NOT NULL, so each bot gets a random, unshared password digest.
  Bots never sign in, and have no email address, so they can't.
- **Management UI:** `BotsController` (`/bots`, `/bots/new`, `/bots/:id/edit`). Reached from the bot icon
  on `/account/edit`, which every member sees.
- **Posting API:** `Bots::MessagesController`, `POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_key/messages`.

## Lifecycle

- **Create:** a new bot joins every open room, the same as a new person (`User#grant_membership_to_open_rooms`).
  Bots can be added to closed rooms through the room forms, like people.
- **Who manages a bot:** the creator, and administrators. The bots page lists the caller's own bots, or
  every bot for an administrator. Anyone else's bot is a 404, not a 403, so its existence isn't revealed.
- **Delete:** `Bot#deactivate` is "delete". It removes the bot from every room (including direct rooms),
  sets `status: deactivated`, and clears `bot_key`. Its past messages stay, as they do for deactivated
  people. A deleted bot's code is a 401.
- **Creator leaves or is banned:** `User#deactivate` and `User::Bannable#ban` deactivate the creator's
  bots. A bot shouldn't outlive the person it's acting for. Unbanning doesn't restore bots.

## Posting API

`POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_key/messages`

| Case | Response |
| --- | --- |
| Posted | `201 Created`, `Location: /messages/:id` |
| Empty or whitespace-only body, no attachment | `422 Unprocessable Content` |
| Unknown, or deleted bot's code | `401 Unauthorized` |
| Room doesn't exist, or the bot isn't a member | `404 Not Found` |

  escaped, and line breaks are kept.

  state and push notifications, the same as for a person's message.

  send tokens and the code is what authenticates them.

# appear as authors like any other user, but they authenticate with a bot code rather than a session.

- The raw body is the message text. No envelope, no field names. Text is stored as plain text: markup is
  escaped, and line breaks are kept.
- Attachments use a multipart upload: an `attachment` file, with optional text in a `body` field.
- Messages are created with `creator: bot`, then `broadcast_create` runs. Room callbacks handle unread
  state and push notifications, the same as for a person's message.
- Auth is the bot code, not a session. CSRF protection is skipped for this controller, since scripts can't
  send tokens and the code is what authenticates them.

### Why the request is special-cased

Two framework behaviours make raw bodies hard, and both are handled deliberately:

1. **`curl -d` sends `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`.** Rails and Rack parse that as form fields, which
   turns `100% done` into a 400 (`invalid %-encoding`). Rack also caches that failure in the request env,
   so re-labelling the request in the controller is too late. `lib/middleware/bot_plain_text_bodies.rb` runs
   before `Rack::MethodOverride`, which is the first thing that parses form bodies, and relabels non-multipart
   bot message POSTs as `text/plain`. `config/application.rb` requires it directly: autoloaded constants aren't
   available there, and `lib/middleware` is excluded from autoloading so the class isn't loaded twice.
2. **The bot code is in the path.** `ActionDispatch::Request#filtered_path` only masks the query string, but
   Rails logs and Sentry report requests with it. `lib/rails_ext/action_dispatch_request.rb` masks the
   segment, so `Started POST "/rooms/1/[FILTERED]/messages"`. Request parameters are masked separately by
   `filter_parameters`, since `_key` matches `bot_key`.

# Bots post their message as the raw request body, which curl sends labelled as form data. Rack and Rails would
# parse that as form fields and fail on text such as "100%", so this relabels bot message bodies as plain text
# before anything reads them as a form. Multipart uploads keep their label, since their attachments need parsing.
class BotPlainTextBodies
  MESSAGES_PATH = %r{\A/rooms/[^/]+/[^/]+/messages\z}

  def initialize(app)
    @app = app
  end

  def call(env)
    if env["REQUEST_METHOD"] == "POST" && MESSAGES_PATH.match?(env["PATH_INFO"]) && !multipart?(env)
      env["CONTENT_TYPE"] = "text/plain"
    end

    @app.call(env)
  end

  private
    def multipart?(env)
      Rack::Request.new(env).media_type == "multipart/form-data"
    end

require "surfguard"

module RestrictedHTTP
  class Violation < StandardError; end

  # The address policy lives in the surfguard gem so this app, Basecamp, HEY and
  # Fizzy classify "internal" the same way instead of each keeping a copy that
  # drifts. The callers here hand a bare hostname in and pin the address that
  # comes back, so this stays a hostname-in, address-out shim.
  module PrivateNetworkGuard
    extend self

    # A hostname that resolves to nothing (NXDOMAIN, timeout, empty answer)
    # raises Surfguard::Unresolvable, which we let propagate as a lookup failure
    # -- the same way the old Resolv.getaddress guard raised Resolv::ResolvError,
    # and the callers here already treat it as a fetch failure. The Violation is
    # reserved for a host that resolves to a blocked address (an empty list back
    # from resolve_public_ips), so a transient DNS miss is never misreported as
    # an SSRF attempt.
    def resolve(hostname)
      Surfguard.resolve_public_ips(hostname).first or
        raise Violation.new("Attempt to access private IP via #{hostname}")
    end

    def private_ip?(ip)
      Surfguard.blocked_address?(ip)
    end
  end
end

    process_attachment_thumbnail

  has_many :memberships, dependent: :delete_all do
    def grant_to(users)
      room = proxy_association.owner
      Membership.insert_all(Array(users).collect { |user| { room_id: room.id, user_id: user.id, involvement: room.default_involvement } })
    end

    def revoke_from(users)
      destroy_by user: users
    end

    def revise(granted: [], revoked: [])
      transaction do
        grant_to(granted) if granted.present?
        revoke_from(revoked) if revoked.present?
      end
    end
  end

  has_many :users, through: :memberships
  has_many :messages, dependent: :destroy

  belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", default: -> { Current.user }

  validate :direct_rooms_keep_their_type, on: :update

  scope :opens,           -> { where(type: "Rooms::Open") }
  scope :closeds,         -> { where(type: "Rooms::Closed") }
  scope :directs,         -> { where(type: "Rooms::Direct") }
  scope :without_directs, -> { where.not(type: "Rooms::Direct") }

  scope :ordered, -> { order("LOWER(name)") }

  class << self
    def create_for(attributes, users:)
      transaction do
        create!(attributes).tap do |room|
          room.memberships.grant_to users
        end
      end
    end

    def original
      order(:created_at).first
    end
  end

  def receive(message)
    unread_memberships(message)
    push_later(message)
  end

  def open?
    is_a?(Rooms::Open)
  end

  def closed?
    is_a?(Rooms::Closed)
  end

  def direct?
    is_a?(Rooms::Direct)
  end

  def default_involvement
    "mentions"
  end

  private
    # Open and closed rooms convert into each other freely. A direct room can't become
    # either: its participants agreed to a private conversation, not to one whose
    # audience someone else gets to widen afterwards.
    def direct_rooms_keep_their_type
      if type_changed? && type_was == "Rooms::Direct"
        errors.add :type, "can't be changed for a direct room"
      end
    end

    def unread_memberships(message)
      memberships.visible.disconnected.where.not(user: message.creator).update_all(unread_at: message.created_at, updated_at: Time.current)
    end

    def push_later(message)
      Room::PushMessageJob.perform_later(self, message)
    end

class Room::MessagePusher
  attr_reader :room, :message

  def initialize(room:, message:)
    @room, @message = room, message
  end

  def push
    build_payload.tap do |payload|
      push_to_users_involved_in_everything(payload)
      push_to_users_involved_in_mentions(payload)
    end
  end

  private
    def build_payload
      if room.direct?
        build_direct_payload
      else
        build_shared_payload
      end
    end

    def build_direct_payload
      {
        title: message.creator.name,
        body: message.plain_text_body,
        path: Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.room_path(room)
      }
    end

    def build_shared_payload
      {
        title: room.name,
        body: "#{message.creator.name}: #{message.plain_text_body}",
        path: Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.room_path(room)
      }
    end

    def push_to_users_involved_in_everything(payload)
      enqueue_payload_for_delivery payload, push_subscriptions_for_users_involved_in_everything
    end

    def push_to_users_involved_in_mentions(payload)
      enqueue_payload_for_delivery payload, push_subscriptions_for_mentionable_users(message.mentionees)
    end

    def push_subscriptions_for_users_involved_in_everything
      relevant_subscriptions.merge(Membership.involved_in_everything)
    end

    def push_subscriptions_for_mentionable_users(mentionees)
      relevant_subscriptions.merge(Membership.involved_in_mentions).where(user_id: mentionees.ids)
    end

    def relevant_subscriptions
      Push::Subscription
        .joins(user: :memberships)
        .merge(Membership.visible.disconnected.where(room: room).where.not(user: message.creator))
    end

    def enqueue_payload_for_delivery(payload, subscriptions)
      Rails.configuration.x.web_push_pool.queue(payload, subscriptions)
    end
end

class Room < ApplicationRecord
  has_many :memberships, dependent: :delete_all do
    def grant_to(users)
      room = proxy_association.owner
      Membership.insert_all(Array(users).collect { |user| { room_id: room.id, user_id: user.id, involvement: room.default_involvement } })
    end

    def revoke_from(users)
      destroy_by user: users
    end

    def revise(granted: [], revoked: [])
      transaction do
        grant_to(granted) if granted.present?
        revoke_from(revoked) if revoked.present?
      end
    end
  end

  has_many :users, through: :memberships
  has_many :messages, dependent: :destroy

  belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", default: -> { Current.user }

  validate :direct_rooms_keep_their_type, on: :update

  scope :opens,           -> { where(type: "Rooms::Open") }
  scope :closeds,         -> { where(type: "Rooms::Closed") }
  scope :directs,         -> { where(type: "Rooms::Direct") }
  scope :without_directs, -> { where.not(type: "Rooms::Direct") }

  scope :ordered, -> { order("LOWER(name)") }

  class << self
    def create_for(attributes, users:)
      transaction do
        create!(attributes).tap do |room|
          room.memberships.grant_to users
        end
      end
    end

    def original
      order(:created_at).first
    end
  end

  def receive(message)
    unread_memberships(message)
    push_later(message)
  end

  def open?
    is_a?(Rooms::Open)
  end

  def closed?
    is_a?(Rooms::Closed)
  end

  def direct?
    is_a?(Rooms::Direct)
  end

  def default_involvement
    "mentions"
  end

  private
    # Open and closed rooms convert into each other freely. A direct room can't become
    # either: its participants agreed to a private conversation, not to one whose
    # audience someone else gets to widen afterwards.
    def direct_rooms_keep_their_type
      if type_changed? && type_was == "Rooms::Direct"
        errors.add :type, "can't be changed for a direct room"
      end
    end

    def unread_memberships(message)
      memberships.visible.disconnected.where.not(user: message.creator).update_all(unread_at: message.created_at, updated_at: Time.current)
    end

    def push_later(message)
      Room::PushMessageJob.perform_later(self, message)
    end
end

class Room::MessagePusher
  attr_reader :room, :message

  def initialize(room:, message:)
    @room, @message = room, message
  end

  def push
    build_payload.tap do |payload|
      push_to_users_involved_in_everything(payload)
      push_to_users_involved_in_mentions(payload)
    end
  end

  private
    def build_payload
      if room.direct?
        build_direct_payload
      else
        build_shared_payload
      end
    end

    def build_direct_payload
      {
        title: message.creator.name,
        body: message.plain_text_body,
        path: Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.room_path(room)
      }
    end

    def build_shared_payload
      {
        title: room.name,
        body: "#{message.creator.name}: #{message.plain_text_body}",
        path: Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.room_path(room)
      }
    end

    def push_to_users_involved_in_everything(payload)
      enqueue_payload_for_delivery payload, push_subscriptions_for_users_involved_in_everything
    end

    def push_to_users_involved_in_mentions(payload)
      enqueue_payload_for_delivery payload, push_subscriptions_for_mentionable_users(message.mentionees)
    end

    def push_subscriptions_for_users_involved_in_everything
      relevant_subscriptions.merge(Membership.involved_in_everything)
    end

    def push_subscriptions_for_mentionable_users(mentionees)
      relevant_subscriptions.merge(Membership.involved_in_mentions).where(user_id: mentionees.ids)
    end

    def relevant_subscriptions
      Push::Subscription
        .joins(user: :memberships)
        .merge(Membership.visible.disconnected.where(room: room).where.not(user: message.creator))
    end

    def enqueue_payload_for_delivery(payload, subscriptions)
      Rails.configuration.x.web_push_pool.queue(payload, subscriptions)
    end
end

# This is in lib so we can use it in a thread pool without the Rails executor
class WebPush::Pool
  attr_reader :delivery_pool, :invalidation_pool, :connection, :invalid_subscription_handler

  def initialize(invalid_subscription_handler:)
    @delivery_pool = Concurrent::ThreadPoolExecutor.new(max_threads: 50, queue_size: 10000)
    @invalidation_pool = Concurrent::FixedThreadPool.new(1)
    @connection = Net::HTTP::Persistent.new(name: "web_push", pool_size: 150)
    @invalid_subscription_handler = invalid_subscription_handler
  end

  def queue(payload, subscriptions)
    subscriptions.find_each do |subscription|
      deliver_later(payload, subscription)
    end
  end

  def shutdown
    connection.shutdown
    shutdown_pool(delivery_pool)
    shutdown_pool(invalidation_pool)
  end

  private
    def deliver_later(payload, subscription)
      # Ensure any AR operations happen before we post to the thread pool
      notification = subscription.notification(**payload)
      subscription_id = subscription.id

      delivery_pool.post do
        deliver(notification, subscription_id)
      rescue Exception => e
        Rails.logger.error "Error in WebPush::Pool.deliver: #{e.class} #{e.message}"
      end
    rescue Concurrent::RejectedExecutionError
    end

    def deliver(notification, id)
      notification.deliver(connection: connection)
    rescue WebPush::ExpiredSubscription, OpenSSL::OpenSSLError => ex
      invalidate_subscription_later(id) if invalid_subscription_handler
    end

    def invalidate_subscription_later(id)
      invalidation_pool.post do
        invalid_subscription_handler.call(id)
      rescue Exception => e
        Rails.logger.error "Error in WebPush::Pool.invalid_subscription_handler: #{e.class} #{e.message}"
      end
    end

    def shutdown_pool(pool)
      pool.shutdown
      pool.kill unless pool.wait_for_termination(1)
    end
end

module WebPush::PersistentRequest
  def perform
    if @options[:connection]
      http = @options[:connection]
    else
      http = Net::HTTP.new(uri.host, uri.port, *proxy_options)
      http.use_ssl = true
      http.ssl_timeout = @options[:ssl_timeout] unless @options[:ssl_timeout].nil?
      http.open_timeout = @options[:open_timeout] unless @options[:open_timeout].nil?
      http.read_timeout = @options[:read_timeout] unless @options[:read_timeout].nil?
    end

    req = Net::HTTP::Post.new(uri.request_uri, headers)
    req.body = body

    if http.is_a?(Net::HTTP::Persistent)
      response = http.request uri, req
    else
      resp = http.request(req)
      verify_response(resp)
    end

    resp
  end
end

require "net/http"
require "restricted_http/private_network_guard"

class Opengraph::Fetch
  ALLOWED_DOCUMENT_CONTENT_TYPE = "text/html"
  MAX_BODY_SIZE = 5.megabytes
  MAX_REDIRECTS = 10

  class TooManyRedirectsError < StandardError; end
  class RedirectDeniedError < StandardError; end

  def fetch_document(url, ip: RestrictedHTTP::PrivateNetworkGuard.resolve(url.host))
    request(url, Net::HTTP::Get, ip: ip) do |response|
      return body_if_acceptable(response)
    end
  end

  def fetch_content_type(url, ip: RestrictedHTTP::PrivateNetworkGuard.resolve(url.host))
    request(url, Net::HTTP::Head, ip: ip) do |response|
      return response["Content-Type"]
    end
  end

  private
    def request(url, request_class, ip:)
      MAX_REDIRECTS.times do
        Net::HTTP.start(url.host, url.port, ipaddr: ip, use_ssl: url.scheme == "https") do |http|
          http.request request_class.new(url) do |response|
            if response.is_a?(Net::HTTPRedirection)
              url, ip = resolve_redirect(response["location"])
            else
              yield response
            end
          end
        end
      end

      raise TooManyRedirectsError

class Opengraph::Fetch
  ALLOWED_DOCUMENT_CONTENT_TYPE = "text/html"
  MAX_BODY_SIZE = 5.megabytes
  MAX_REDIRECTS = 10

  class TooManyRedirectsError < StandardError; end
  class RedirectDeniedError < StandardError; end

  def fetch_document(url, ip: RestrictedHTTP::PrivateNetworkGuard.resolve(url.host))
    request(url, Net::HTTP::Get, ip: ip) do |response|
      return body_if_acceptable(response)
    end
  end

  def fetch_content_type(url, ip: RestrictedHTTP::PrivateNetworkGuard.resolve(url.host))
    request(url, Net::HTTP::Head, ip: ip) do |response|
      return response["Content-Type"]
    end
  end

  private
    def request(url, request_class, ip:)
      MAX_REDIRECTS.times do
        Net::HTTP.start(url.host, url.port, ipaddr: ip, use_ssl: url.scheme == "https") do |http|
          http.request request_class.new(url) do |response|
            if response.is_a?(Net::HTTPRedirection)

class ContentFilters::RemoveSoloUnfurledLinkText < ActionText::Content::Filter
  def applicable?
    normalize_tweet_url(solo_unfurled_url) == normalize_tweet_url(content.to_plain_text)
  end

  def apply
    fragment.replace("div") { |node| node.tap { |n| n.inner_html = unfurled_links.first.to_s } }
  end

  private
    TWITTER_DOMAINS = %w[ x.com twitter.com ]
    TWITTER_DOMAIN_MAPPING = { "x.com" => "twitter.com" }

    def solo_unfurled_url
      unfurled_links.first["href"] if unfurled_links.size == 1
    end

    def unfurled_links
      fragment.find_all("action-text-attachment[@content-type='#{ActionText::Attachment::OpengraphEmbed::OPENGRAPH_EMBED_CONTENT_TYPE}']")
    end

    def normalize_tweet_url(url)
      return url unless twitter_url?(url)

      uri = URI.parse(url)

      uri.dup.tap do |u|
        u.host = TWITTER_DOMAIN_MAPPING[uri.host&.downcase] || uri.host
        u.query = nil
      end.to_s
    rescue URI::InvalidURIError
      url
    end

    def twitter_url?(url)
      url.present? && TWITTER_DOMAINS.any? { |domain| url.strip.include?(domain) }
    end
end
class ContentFilters::SanitizeAttributes < ActionText::Content::Filter
  def applicable?
    true
  end

  # Scrub attributes on the tags that SanitizeTags allows, using Rails' safe-list
  # sanitizer so unsafe URI schemes and event-handler attributes are stripped.
  # Runs after SanitizeTags, so passing the same allowed tags makes the tag pass
  # a no-op and only attributes are scrubbed.
  def apply
    sanitizer.sanitize fragment.to_html, tags: allowed_tags, attributes: allowed_attributes
  end

  private
    # Presentation styling relies on class attributes (e.g. unfurled link embeds),
    # which the standard ActionText set doesn't include.
    EXTRA_ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES = %w[ class ]

    # ActionText::ContentHelper.sanitizer is a single process-wide instance, and
    # rails-html-sanitizer reuses one mutable permit scrubber that it reconfigures
    # from the tags/attributes on every #sanitize call. Sharing it here would race
    # our stricter tag set against ActionText's default rendering on concurrent
    # requests, so use a dedicated instance of the same sanitizer class to keep the
    # scrubber isolated.
    def sanitizer
      sanitizer_class.new
    end

    def sanitizer_class
      ActionText::ContentHelper.sanitizer.class
    end

    def allowed_tags
      ContentFilters::SanitizeTags::ALLOWED_TAGS
    end

    def allowed_attributes
      standard_allowed_attributes + EXTRA_ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES
    end

    # Mirrors ActionText::ContentHelper#sanitizer_allowed_attributes, which isn't
    # exposed at the module level.
    def standard_allowed_attributes
      ActionText::ContentHelper.allowed_attributes ||
        (sanitizer_class.allowed_attributes + ActionText::Attachment::ATTRIBUTES).to_a
    end
end
class ContentFilters::SanitizeTags < ActionText::Content::Filter
  def applicable?
    true
  end

  def apply
    fragment.replace(not_allowed_tags_css_selector) { nil }
  end

  private
    ALLOWED_TAGS = %w[ a abbr acronym address b big blockquote br cite code dd del dfn div dl dt em h1 h2 h3 h4 h5 h6 hr i ins kbd li ol
      p pre samp small span strong sub sup time tt ul var ] + [ ActionText::Attachment.tag_name, "figure", "figcaption" ]

    def not_allowed_tags_css_selector
      ALLOWED_TAGS.map { |tag| ":not(#{tag})" }.join("")
    end
end
class ContentFilters::StyleUnfurledTwitterAvatars < ActionText::Content::Filter
  def applicable?
    unfurled_twitter_avatars.present?
  end

  def apply
    fragment.update do |source|
      div = source.at_css("div")
      div["class"] = UNFURLED_TWITTER_AVATAR_CSS_CLASS
    end
  end

  private
    UNFURLED_TWITTER_AVATAR_CSS_CLASS = "cf-twitter-avatar"
    TWITTER_AVATAR_URL_PREFIX = "https://pbs.twimg.com/profile_images"

    def unfurled_twitter_avatars
      fragment.find_all("#{opengraph_css_selector}[url*='#{TWITTER_AVATAR_URL_PREFIX}']")

  end

  def apply

  end

class ContentFilters::StyleUnfurledTwitterAvatars < ActionText::Content::Filter
  def applicable?

  end

class BotTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    @creator = users(:david)
  end

  test "creating a bot gives it a bot code and an unguessable password it never uses" do
    bot = create_bot

    assert_match(/\A[[:alnum:]]{32}\z/, bot.bot_key)
    assert bot.password_digest.present?
    assert_nil bot.email_address
  end

  test "bot codes are unique" do
    bot = create_bot
    duplicate = Bot.new(name: "Copycat", creator: @creator, bot_key: bot.bot_key)

    assert_not duplicate.valid?
    assert duplicate.errors[:bot_key].any?
  end

  test "bot names are required" do
    bot = Bot.new(name: "", creator: @creator)

    assert_not bot.valid?
    assert bot.errors[:name].any?
  end

  test "creating a bot grants it membership to the open rooms but not to closed rooms" do
    closed_room = rooms(:designers)
    closed_room.update!(type: "Rooms::Closed")

    bot = create_bot

    assert_equal Rooms::Open.count, bot.rooms.opens.count
    assert_not bot.rooms.include?(closed_room)
  end

  test "bots are listed as the creator's bots" do
    bot = create_bot

    assert_includes @creator.bots, bot
    assert_not_includes users(:jason).bots, bot
  end

  test "bots are left out of the people scope" do
    bot = create_bot

    assert_includes User.all, bot
    assert_not_includes User.humans, bot
    assert_includes User.humans, users(:david)
  end

  test "deactivating a bot removes it from its rooms, clears its code and keeps its messages" do

    message = rooms(:watercooler).messages.create!(creator: bot, body: "Deploy finished")

  end

  has_many :boosts, dependent: :destroy, foreign_key: :booster_id
  has_many :searches, dependent: :delete_all

  has_many :sessions, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :bans, dependent: :destroy

  has_many :bots, foreign_key: :creator_id, inverse_of: :creator

  enum :status, %i[ active deactivated banned ], default: :active

  has_secure_password validations: false

  after_create_commit :grant_membership_to_open_rooms

  scope :ordered, -> { order("LOWER(name)") }
  scope :filtered_by, ->(query) { where("name like ?", "%#{query}%") }

  # Everyone who isn't a bot. Bots are managed on their own page, so people-only lists leave them out.
  scope :humans, -> { where(type: nil) }

  def initials
    name.scan(/\b\w/).join
  end

  def title
    [ name, bio ].compact_blank.join(" – ")
  end

  def deactivate
    transaction do
      close_remote_connections

      memberships.without_direct_rooms.delete_all
      push_subscriptions.delete_all
      searches.delete_all
      sessions.delete_all
      deactivate_bots

      update! status: :deactivated, email_address: deactived_email_address
    end
  end

  def bot?
    is_a?(Bot)
  end

  def reset_remote_connections
    close_remote_connections reconnect: true
  end

    # A bot is only as trustworthy as the person who created it, so its bots stop working along with them.
    def deactivate_bots
      bots.active.each(&:deactivate)

# Rooms for direct message chats between users. These act as a singleton, so a single set of users will
# always refer to the same direct room.
class Rooms::Direct < Room
  class << self
    def find_or_create_for(users)
      find_for(users) || create_for({}, users: users)
    end

    private
      # FIXME: Find a more performant algorithm that won't be a problem on accounts with 10K+ direct rooms,
      # which could be to store the membership id list as a hash on the room, and use that for lookup.
      def find_for(users)
        all.joins(:users).detect do |room|
          Set.new(room.user_ids) == Set.new(users.pluck(:id))
        end
      end
  end

  def default_involvement

# Rooms for direct message chats between users. These act as a singleton, so a single set of users will
# always refer to the same direct room.
class Rooms::Direct < Room
  class << self
    def find_or_create_for(users)
      find_for(users) || create_for({}, users: users)
    end

    private
      # FIXME: Find a more performant algorithm that won't be a problem on accounts with 10K+ direct rooms,
      # which could be to store the membership id list as a hash on the room, and use that for lookup.
      def find_for(users)
        all.joins(:users).detect do |room|
          Set.new(room.user_ids) == Set.new(users.pluck(:id))
        end
      end
  end

  def default_involvement
    "everything"
  end
end

  test "grant membership to user" do

messages.content:
I have what I need to design this. Before writing code, here's the plan:

- **Storage:** a `users.webhook_url` column (bots are STI rows in `users`), normalized so blank means "no webhook", and validated as http(s).
- **Trigger:** `Room#receive` runs after commit. For each mentioned bot that has a webhook, it enqueues a `Bot::WebhookJob`, so the poster's request never waits on HTTP. Bot-authored messages never trigger webhooks, which prevents bot-to-bot loops.
- **Delivery:** `Bot::Webhook` POSTs JSON with a short timeout, resolves the host through the existing `RestrictedHTTP` guard and pins the IP (the same SSRF defence used for link unfurling), and doesn't follow redirects. A 200 with a text body is posted back into the room. The response is size-capped, because a bot's response becomes a chat message.
- **Reuse:** the existing posting API and the webhook reply share one "post as bot" path.

I'll write the failing tests first to pin down the behaviour, starting with the model layer. I'll also extend the mention test helper so it accepts bot records.

require "net/http"
require "restricted_http/private_network_guard"

# Calls a bot's webhook to say that someone mentioned it, then posts the bot's answer into the room, if it gave one.
#
# This runs in a background job, so the person who posted the mention never waits on it. Redirects aren't followed,
# and the webhook's host is resolved and checked against private networks before connecting, as link unfurling is.
# A bot's answer becomes a message, so only a 200 with a text body counts, and it's limited in size.
class Bot::Webhook
  OPEN_TIMEOUT = 5
  READ_TIMEOUT = 10
  MAX_REPLY_SIZE = 64.kilobytes
  REPLY_CONTENT_TYPES = %w[ text/plain text/html ]

  class ReplyTooLargeError < StandardError; end

  attr_reader :bot, :message
  delegate :room, to: :message

  def initialize(bot:, message:)
    @bot, @message = bot, message
  end

  def deliver
    return unless deliverable?

    reply = request_reply
    post_reply(reply) if reply
  end

  private
    # The bot may have been removed from the room, deactivated or lost its webhook since the mention was posted.
    def deliverable?
      bot.active? && bot.webhook_url.present? && bot.rooms.exists?(room.id)
    end

    def request_reply
      reply = nil

      connect do |http|
        http.request(build_request) do |response|
          reply = read_reply(response) if response.is_a?(Net::HTTPOK)
        end
      end

      reply
    rescue StandardError => e
      Rails.logger.warn "Failed to call the webhook for bot #{bot.id} about message #{message.id} (#{e.class}: #{e.message})"
      nil
    end

    def connect(&)
      uri = webhook_uri
      ip = RestrictedHTTP::PrivateNetworkGuard.resolve(uri.host)

      Net::HTTP.start uri.host, uri.port, ipaddr: ip, use_ssl: uri.scheme == "https",
        open_timeout: OPEN_TIMEOUT, read_timeout: READ_TIMEOUT, &
    end

    def build_request
      Net::HTTP::Post.new(webhook_uri.request_uri, "Content-Type" => "application/json").tap do |request|
        request.body = payload.to_json
      end
    end

    def read_reply(response)
      content_type = response.content_type&.downcase
      return unless REPLY_CONTENT_TYPES.include?(content_type)

      body = String.new
      response.read_body do |chunk|
        body << chunk
        raise ReplyTooLargeError if body.bytesize > MAX_REPLY_SIZE
      end

      { content_type: content_type, text: decode(body, response.type_params["charset"]) }
    end

    def decode(bytes, charset)
      encoding = Encoding.find(charset) rescue Encoding::UTF_8
      bytes.force_encoding(encoding).encode(Encoding::UTF_8, invalid: :replace, undef: :replace).scrub
    end

    def post_reply(reply)
      text = reply[:text].strip
      body = reply[:content_type] == "text/html" ? text : Bot.html_from_plain_text(text)

      return if body.blank? || ActionText::Content.new(body).to_plain_text.blank?

      bot.post_message(room, body: body)
    end

    def payload
      {
        event: "mention",
        author: { id: message.creator.id, name: message.creator.name },
        room: { id: room.id, name: room.name, reply_to: routes.bot_messages_path(room, bot.bot_key) },
        message: {
          id: message.id,
          body: { text: text, html: html },
          link: routes.room_at_message_path(room, message)
        }
      }
    end

    # The mention of the bot itself is removed, so the text reads as the command addressed to the bot.
    def text
      without_own_mention = message.body.body.fragment.replace(ActionText::Attachment.tag_name) do |node|
        node unless ActionText::Attachable.from_node(node) == bot
      end

      ActionText::Content.new(without_own_mention, canonicalize: false).to_plain_text.gsub(/[ \t]{2,}/, " ").strip
    end

    # The whole body as it's displayed, so the bot's own mention is kept here.
    def html
      ContentFilters::TextMessagePresentationFilters.apply(message.body.body).to_s
    end

    def webhook_uri
      URI.parse(bot.webhook_url)
    end

    def routes
      Rails.application.routes.url_helpers
    end
end
EOF

  # If the bot or the message is gone by the time the job runs, there's nothing left to deliver.
  discard_on ActiveJob::DeserializationError

  def perform(bot, message)
    Bot::Webhook.new(bot: bot, message: message).deliver
  end
end

# Lets bots post from scripts and CI jobs, so it doesn't use sessions or CSRF tokens. The bot code in the path
# is the only credential, and the request body is taken as the message as-is.
class Bots::MessagesController < ApplicationController
  include ActiveStorage::SetCurrent

  allow_unauthenticated_access
  skip_forgery_protection

  rescue_from(ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound) { head :not_found }

  before_action :set_bot
  before_action :set_room

  def create
    if message_text.blank? && attachment.blank?
      head :unprocessable_content
    else
      message = @bot.post_message(@room, body: Bot.html_from_plain_text(message_text), attachment: attachment)

      head :created, location: message_path(message)
    end
  end

  private
    def set_bot
      @bot = Bot.active.find_by(bot_key: params[:bot_key])
      head :unauthorized unless @bot
    end

    # Bots only get rooms they're members of. Rooms they aren't in look just like rooms that don't exist.
    def set_room
      @room = @bot.rooms.find(params[:room_id])
    end

    # A raw body is the message. Attachments need multipart uploads, so their text comes from a body field instead.
    def message_text
      @message_text ||= begin

Before the full suite, I want to tighten one thing in the request path. `mentioned_bots` currently runs a query for every new message, even ones with no mentions. I'll short-circuit when the message mentions no bot, using the attachables already resolved in memory.

cd /app && cat > app/models/message/mentionee.rb <<'EOF'
module Message::Mentionee
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  def mentionees
    room.users.where(id: mentioned_users.map(&:id))
  end

  # Bots in the room that were mentioned and have a webhook to call. Most messages mention no bots, so they skip the query.

class BotsController < ApplicationController
  # Bot codes and webhook URLs are credentials, so the pages that show them must never be stored by browsers or caches.
  before_action :prevent_caching, except: :destroy
  before_action :set_bot, only: %i[ edit update destroy ]

  def index
    @bots = visible_bots.ordered
  end

  def new
    @bot = Bot.new
  end

  def create
    @bot = Current.user.bots.build(bot_params)

    if @bot.save
      redirect_to bots_url
    else
      flash.now[:alert] = @bot.errors.full_messages.to_sentence
      render :new, status: :unprocessable_content
    end
  end

  def edit
  end

  def update
    if @bot.update(bot_params)
      redirect_to bots_url
    else
      flash.now[:alert] = @bot.errors.full_messages.to_sentence
      render :edit, status: :unprocessable_content
    end
  end

  def destroy
    @bot.deactivate
    redirect_to bots_url
  end

  private
    def prevent_caching
      response.cache_control.merge! no_store: true
    end

    # Administrators manage every bot; everyone else only the bots they created. Bots outside that
    # set are reported as missing rather than forbidden, so their existence isn't revealed.
    def visible_bots
      Current.user.administrator? ? Bot.active : Current.user.bots.active
    end

    def set_bot
      @bot = visible_bots.find(params[:id])
    end

    # A blank avatar means no new one was chosen, so it must not clear the existing one.
    def bot_params
      params.require(:bot).permit(:name, :avatar, :webhook_url).tap do |attributes|
        attributes.delete(:avatar) if attributes[:avatar].blank?
      end
    end
end

require "restricted_http/private_network_guard"

# Calls a bot's webhook to say that someone mentioned it, then posts the bot's answer into the room, if it gave one.
#
# This runs in a background job, so the person who posted the mention never waits on it. Redirects aren't followed,
# and the webhook's host is resolved and checked against private networks before connecting, as link unfurling is.
# A bot's answer becomes a message, so only a 200 with a text body counts, and it's limited in size.
class Bot::Webhook
  OPEN_TIMEOUT = 5
  READ_TIMEOUT = 10
  MAX_REPLY_SIZE = 64.kilobytes
  REPLY_CONTENT_TYPES = %w[ text/plain text/html ]

  class ReplyTooLargeError < StandardError; end

  attr_reader :bot, :message
  delegate :room, to: :message

  def initialize(bot:, message:)
    @bot, @message = bot, message
  end

  def deliver
    return unless deliverable?

    reply = request_reply
    post_reply(reply) if reply
  end

  private
    # The bot may have been removed from the room, deactivated or lost its webhook since the mention was posted.
    def deliverable?
      bot.active? && bot.webhook_url.present? && bot.rooms.exists?(room.id)
    end

    def request_reply
      reply = nil

      connect do |http|
        http.request(build_request) do |response|
          reply = read_reply(response) if response.is_a?(Net::HTTPOK)
        end
      end

      reply
    rescue StandardError => e
      Rails.logger.warn "Failed to call the webhook for bot #{bot.id} about message #{message.id} (#{e.class}: #{e.message})"
      nil
    end

    def connect(&)
      uri = webhook_uri
      ip = RestrictedHTTP::PrivateNetworkGuard.resolve(uri.host)

      Net::HTTP.start uri.host, uri.port, ipaddr: ip, use_ssl: uri.scheme == "https",
        open_timeout: OPEN_TIMEOUT, read_timeout: READ_TIMEOUT, &
    end

    def build_request
      Net::HTTP::Post.new(webhook_uri.request_uri, "Content-Type" => "application/json").tap do |request|
        request.body = payload.to_json
      end
    end

    def read_reply(response)
      content_type = response.content_type&.downcase

  READ_TIMEOUT = 10
  MAX_REPLY_SIZE = 64.kilobytes
  REPLY_CONTENT_TYPES = %w[ text/plain text/html ]

  class ReplyTooLargeError < StandardError; end

  delegate :room, to: :message

  def initialize(bot:, message:)
    @bot, @message = bot, message

    return unless deliverable?

    reply = request_reply
    post_reply(reply) if reply
  end

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "## How it fits together

- **Bots are users.** `Bot < User`, a single-table-inheritance subclass stored in the `users` table
  (`users.type = 'Bot'`). Memberships, message authorship, avatars, mentions, unread tracking and push
...
- **Delete:** `Bot#deactivate` is "delete". It removes the bot from every room (including direct rooms),
  sets `status: deactivated`, and clears `bot_key`. Its past messages stay, as they do for deactivated
  people. A deleted bot's code is a 401.
...
## Security notes

The bot code is a credential. It's stored in plaintext, because the bots page has to show it again later.
Given that:

- **Visibility:** only the creator and administrators see a bot's code. It's shown on the bots list only,
  not on the edit page. Bots have no JSON representation.
- **Caching:** the bots index responds with `Cache-Control: no-store`, and carries
  `<meta name="turbo-cache-control" content="no-cache">` so Turbo doesn't keep a snapshot of it.
- **Logs:** Rails request logs and parameter logs mask the code (see above).
- **Known gap, SQL logs:** the development log includes bot codes inline in SQL statements (`WHERE bot_key = '…'`).
  Session tokens and password digests already appear the same way, so this follows the existing posture. Masking
  it would mean filtering the SQL log, or encrypting the column with ActiveRecord encryption (which needs keys).
- **Reverse proxies and access logs** record the request path, including the code. Operators should filter
  `/rooms/*/*/messages` out of proxy logs.
- **Lookup:** `Bot.active.find_by(bot_key:)`, the same shape as session token lookup.
...
## Known gaps and follow-ups

- **`Location` points at a route that 404s for GET.** `/messages/:id` is the top-level message route,
  which `MessagesController` only uses for nested boosts. Its `show` runs the room-scoped `set_room`, so
  it 404s. Room-scoped `/rooms/:room_id/messages/:id` works. The spec fixes `Location`, so it's left
  as-is. A permalink redirect (top-level show → `room_at_message_path`) would fix it.
- **No code rotation.** Regenerating a bot code means deleting the bot and creating a new one. Adding a
  "regenerate code" action would be a `bot_key` reset plus a confirm.
- **Bot messages can only be edited or deleted by administrators,** not the bot's creator, since authorship
  is the bot. Widen `Current.user.can_administer?(message)` if creators should be able to moderate their bots.
- **No rate limiting** on the posting endpoint. A leaked code can post freely until it's deleted.
- **No size limit:** nothing caps the message size beyond the server's own request limits.

## Testing

- Model (including the creator-deactivation and ban cascades): `test/models/bot_test.rb`.
- Management UI: `test/controllers/bots_controller_test.rb`.
- Posting API: `test/controllers/bots/messages_controller_test.rb`, including CSRF protection left on and the
  log-filtered parameters.
- Framework glue: `test/lib/middleware/bot_plain_text_bodies_test.rb`, `test/lib/rails_ext/action_dispatch_request_test.rb`.
- Browser system tests can't run where ChromeDriver can't be downloaded. The management flow and the posting
  path were checked by driving headless Chromium against a development server.
"
}

Edits don't trigger it, the same as push notifications. `Room#receive` enqueues one `Bot::WebhookJob` per mentioned bot, after the message commits. - **Never in the request:** posting only enqueues the job. The HTTP call runs in the background (Resque in production), so a slow or broken bot can't slow the poster down. - **Bots don't trigger bots:** a message from a bot never calls webhooks, or two bots that mention each other would loop. - **Request:** `POST` with `Content-Type: application/json`: ```json { "event": "mention", "author": { "id": 7, "name": "Alice" }, "room": { "id": 5, "name": "Ops", "reply_to": "/rooms/5//messages" }, "message": { "id": 118, "body": { "text": "restart the build please", "html": "

" }, "link": "/rooms/5/@118" } } ``` - `event` is always `mention` for now. More event types may come later. - `message.body.text` is the plain text with the bot's own mention removed, so it reads as the command addressed to the bot. Mentions of other people stay, as `@Name`. - `message.body.html` is the whole rich text body, sanitized the way it's displayed. The bot's own mention stays in it. - `room.reply_to` is the bot's own posting URL for that room. The bot replies out-of-band with the posting API. - `message.link` opens the room scrolled to the message. - Paths are relative. The bot knows its Campfire origin. ### Replies | Response | Result | | --- | --- | | `200` with `Content-Type: text/plain` | The body is posted into the room as the bot's message. It's escaped, and line breaks are kept, the same as the posting API. | | `200` with `Content-Type: text/html` | The body is posted as rich text, sanitized before it's stored. | | `204` | Nothing is posted. | | Anything else: other statuses, other content types, redirects, timeouts | Nothing is posted. The failure is logged at warn level. | - A reply that's empty or only whitespace counts as no reply. - A reply over 64 KB is dropped, so a misbehaving bot can't store huge messages. - Redirects aren't followed, and nothing is retried, since a retry could post a second reply. - A reply is an ordinary message from the bot.
